In the USA, if a copyright infringement case has been decided by the judicial system to be fair use, is it more accurate to say that a) copyright infringement occurred but it was legally excused, or b) copyright infringement did not occur?

message.content: More accurate: b, in the legal sense. Fair use means no copyright infringement. A court may say that use is lawful; therefore no actionable copyright infringement exists. This is not an excuse after wrongdoing. Copying may happen, yet fair use blocks infringement.
